newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber unchanged in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber unchanged in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian SIR20 rubber prices were unchanged in late trading on Friday as the market continued to suffer from poor buying interest, traders said.
They said a few inquiries were reported in the afternoon, but traders were unwilling to sell because prices were too low.
"No trading took place today as the market continued to drift without any direction. Nobody seems to be interested in doing any purchasing," said one trader.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 46.75 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan for May/June shipment, 46.25 fob Padang, 46.50 fob Surabaya, 46.00 fob Jambi and 45.75 fob Pontianak.
"Buyers want to buy rubber at at least 45.25, but traders think it is not profitable for them. The only thing which makes us feel better is the end of the strike at Goodyear," said another trader.
"We expect an improvement in rubber prices next week because of Goodyear," he added.
Traders have predicted this week that sluggish consumer demand could push rubber prices down to as low as 45.00 U.S. cents/lb.
